previous_lessons: Legacy migrations fail when you treat the code as the source of truth while ignoring the undocumented side effects in the database.
A constrained pool creates a predictable system.
A container limit is a hard ceiling for the entire process, not just your heap; always leave a 25% buffer for the JVM's internal tax.
A system that knows when to say no is more resilient than one that tries to do everything until it dies.
Caching is a temporary mask for architectural debt that eventually defaults during peak load.
Architectural separation is about logical boundaries, not necessarily adding more moving parts.
Idempotency must be guaranteed by hard database constraints, not transient cache layers that can silently evict keys under pressure.
Strict, boring API contracts protect systems from human drift far better than any post-incident postmortem ever can.
Database schema evolution must be decoupled into multi-phase, non-locking rollouts to avoid catastrophic table locks under concurrent production load.
